examples.text: Называется съедобное меню, хочу у себя ввести.
examples.trans: It is called an edible menu, I want to introduce it at my place.

examples.text: О нашем новом съедобном меню, вы помните?
examples.trans: About our new edible menu, do you remember?

examples.text: Элеонора сказала, что нужно сделать съедобное меню.
examples.trans: Eleonora said that we need to make an edible menu.

meanings.note: A whole portion; completed action. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ъесть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to eat (up)', paired with 'есть'.

examples.text: Скоро. А пока я есть хочу, слона бы съел!
examples.trans: Soon. But for now I'm hungry, I could eat an elephant!

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Core Russian pron meaning 'such, like this' in everyday speech.
там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.
examples.trans: I don't remember his exact address.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Дай хоть одну = give me just one. Core Russian part meaning 'at least, just' in everyday speech.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: + past tense: 'чтобы свидетели были'
+ infinitive. Core Russian conj meaning 'so that, in order to' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm calling to say thank you.
So that there are witnesses, Samson.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'thing; piece' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А жизнь — сложная штука. Вы понимаете, о чём я?
examples.trans: And life is a complicated thing. Do you understand what I am talking about?
And life is a complicated thing.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
